newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Angola to offer ultra-deep oil blocks in a month.
newsitem.headline: Angola to offer ultra-deep oil blocks in a month.

text.p: Angola plans to invite bids for its ultra-deep offshore oil blocks in a month in a bid to boost oil production from the current 715,000 barrels per day, Angola's National Director of Petroleum Jose Manguera said on Wednesday.
He said Angola had tremendous potential and was already the largest oil producer in southern Africa but more investments and exploration were needed if it was to realise its full capacity.

"The (exploration) results of 1996 and 1997 confirm this high petroleum potential with the discovery of reserves we estimate at more than four billion barrels," Manguera told delegates at a sub-Saharan Oil and Minerals conference.
He said production had increased to 715,000 bpd from 173,000 bpd in 1974 after independence from Portugal.
Angola has said it aims to produce a million barrels per day by the year 2000.
Manguera said there were still many available and unexplored areas both offshore and onshore.

"The Kwanza onshore area, where the first commercial field was discovered in 1955, has seen no exploration work since 1975 and the Cassange, Etosha an Okawango interior basins are still virgin of petroleum exploration."
He said in shallow offshore areas, a number of blocks were still available for exploration.
"Due to the considerable potential of these blocks, bidder competition has been great," Manguera said, adding that the first ultra-deep blocks would be offered for bidding in a month.
Angola could become the largest supplier of refined petroleum products to southern Africa if it had the required refining capacity.
Manguera said the construction of a refinery to supply southern Africa was a project which had been kept in limbo since 1975, but which could be revived with foreign investment.
"The studies (that) have been done about a new refinery suggest a cracking catalytic refinery for 200,000 bpd will be adequate for local and regional markets."
He said the country's petroleum law was currently being revised.

"The purpose of this revision is to make the petroleum (industry) more flexible and adapted to the market economy, in an effort to catch the eye of and pave the way for private initiative and foreign investment."
